# Introduction

This analysis investigates propensity score matching in patients based on PD-L1 expression and other clinical parameters.

# Loading Libraries

```{r dataLoad,warning=F, message=F,eval=TRUE}
# Loading CSV file with patient info
# Load required libraries
library(data.table)
library(stringr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(MatchIt)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(survey)
library(compareGroups)
library(cobalt)
library(ggsurvfit)
library(openxlsx)
library(knitr)
source("Scripts/PSM_survival_function.R")

```

## Pre-processing of data

* Check that all columns have no spaces etc, especially character columns, 
* transform character columns to factors. 
* Check if all factors are ok.
* Check numerical columns.

We first need to define which columns we want as character (categorical), and which need to be numerical. Sometimes things get messed up with excel files.

```{r,warning=F, message=F,eval=TRUE}
# Column transformations for consistency
# setwd("")
dataDF <- read.xlsx(xlsxFile = "Data/Post-TIL_BRAF_propensity_matching.xlsx", check.names = T)

# Check for duplicates
any(duplicated(dataDF$patient_id))

# Remove duplicates
dataDF <- dataDF[!duplicated(dataDF), ]

## HERE we define for which parameters we want to do univariate analysis, and which to include in the multivariate survival analysis.
## PLEASE define name as it is on the csv file, the name needs to be in BRACKETS
features <- c("ECOG.PS", "LDH.elevated.","CNS.metastases","Treatment.line","Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL")

## Define which columns include survival data
OS_time <- c("OS.months")
OS_status <- c("OS.event")
PFS_time <- c("PFS.months")
PFS_status <- c("PFS.event")

## DEFINE IF YOU ARE DOING OS OR PFS
surv_time <- PFS_time
surv_status <- PFS_status
surv_time_label <- "PFS"

# KM plots labels
xlabel=".PFS.days"

## DEFINE WHICH COLUMNS ARE CATEGORICAL
categ_feats <-setdiff(features, c("ECOG.PS"))

## DEFINE WHICH COLUMNS ARE NUMERICAL
# we also add the status and time columns
numeric_feats <- c(OS_time,OS_status,PFS_time,PFS_status, setdiff(features, categ_feats))

## FIRST MAKE SURE THERE ARE NO BLANKS ANYWHERE IN THE DATA
## Find non-Numeric columns
num_cols <- unlist(lapply(dataDF, is.numeric))         

dataDF <- cbind(apply(dataDF[,!num_cols], 2, str_remove_all, "NA"),dataDF[,num_cols])   

### NOW MAKE SURE THAT THE COLUMNS ARE IN THE CORRECT FORMAT NEEDED FOR ANALYSIS.
## Numeric columns
dataDF <- dataDF %>% mutate(across(all_of(numeric_feats), as.numeric))

## Categorical
dataDF <- dataDF %>% mutate(across(all_of(categ_feats), as.character))

# We need to transform character columns to categorical, to have the different levels
dataDF <- dataDF %>% mutate(across(all_of(categ_feats), as.factor))
dataDF <- dataDF %>% select(all_of(c(colnames(dataDF)[1], OS_time,OS_status, PFS_time,PFS_status, features))) %>% distinct()

dim(dataDF)

# To remove both (NAs):
dataDF <- dataDF %>% drop_na

#code LDH column
dataDF <- dataDF %>% dplyr::mutate(
    LDH.elevated. = case_when(
      LDH.elevated. == "No"  ~ "0",
      LDH.elevated. == "Yes"  ~ "1",
      LDH.elevated. == "Unknown"  ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    LDH.elevated. = factor(
      LDH.elevated.,
      levels = c("1", "0")
    )
)

dim(dataDF)

table(dataDF$Treatment.line)

table(dataDF$Treatment.line, dataDF$Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL)

## LET's LOOK AT A SUMMARY OF THE DATA
summary(dataDF)
```

```{r Massaging dammed data}
# Column transformations for consistency
dataDF_dammed <- fread("Data/udtræks_forsøg_KM04042025_metast.csv")
#only BRAF/MEK treated patients
dataDF_dammed <- subset(dataDF_dammed, regime_id_combined %in% c("BRAF/MEK inhibitors"))
# Remove duplicates
dataDF_dammed <- dataDF_dammed[-which(duplicated(dataDF_dammed$record_id)),]
#keep only > 1 line patients
dataDF_dammed <- subset(dataDF_dammed, line_therapy > 1)

#calculate age
dataDF_dammed$regime_start_date_correct <- as.Date(dataDF_dammed$regime_start_date, format = "%d-%m-%Y")
dataDF_dammed$birthdate_correct <- as.Date(dataDF_dammed$birthdate, format = "%d-%m-%Y")
dataDF_dammed$age <- difftime(dataDF_dammed$regime_start_date_correct, dataDF_dammed$birthdate_correct)/365

#calculate os
dataDF_dammed$date_last_alive <- as.Date(dataDF_dammed$date_last_alive, format = "%d-%m-%Y")
dataDF_dammed$date_death <- as.Date(dataDF_dammed$date_death, format = "%d-%m-%Y")
dataDF_dammed <- dataDF_dammed %>%
  mutate(
    date_OS_calc = coalesce(date_last_alive, date_death)      # take a unless it’s NA, otherwise b
  )
dataDF_dammed$OS.months <- difftime(dataDF_dammed$date_OS_calc, dataDF_dammed$regime_start_date_correct, units = "days")/30.44

dataDF_dammed$date_progression <- as.Date(dataDF_dammed$date_progression, format = "%d-%m-%Y")
dataDF_dammed$date_seen_no_progression <- as.Date(dataDF_dammed$date_seen_no_progression, format = "%d-%m-%Y")
dataDF_dammed <- dataDF_dammed %>%
  mutate(
    date_PFS_calc = coalesce(date_progression, date_seen_no_progression)      # take a unless it’s NA, otherwise b
  )
dataDF_dammed$PFS.months <- difftime(dataDF_dammed$date_PFS_calc, dataDF_dammed$regime_start_date_correct,units = "days")/30.44

#code OS and PFS events
dataDF_dammed <- dataDF_dammed %>% dplyr::mutate(
  OS.event = case_when(
    is.na(dataDF_dammed$date_death)  ~ "0",
    !(is.na(dataDF_dammed$date_death))  ~ "1",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ),
  OS.event = factor(
    OS.event,
    levels = c("1", "0")
  ),
  PFS.event = case_when(
    !(is.na(dataDF_dammed$date_progression))  ~ "1",
    !(is.na(dataDF_dammed$date_death))  ~ "1",
    is.na(dataDF_dammed$date_progression) & is.na(dataDF_dammed$date_death) ~ "0",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ),
  PFS.event = factor(
    PFS.event,
    levels = c("1", "0")
)
)

#code LDH column
dataDF_dammed <- dataDF_dammed %>% dplyr::mutate(
    LDH.elevated. = case_when(
      ldh > 255 & age >= 70  ~ "1",
      ldh < 255 & age >= 70  ~ "0",
      ldh > 205 & age < 70  ~ "1",
      ldh < 205 & age < 70  ~ "0",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    LDH.elevated. = factor(
      LDH.elevated.,
      levels = c("1", "0")
    )
)

#rename columns of interest
names(dataDF_dammed)[names(dataDF_dammed) == 'performance_status'] <- 'ECOG.PS'
names(dataDF_dammed)[names(dataDF_dammed) == 'metastasis_brain___1'] <- 'CNS.metastases'
names(dataDF_dammed)[names(dataDF_dammed) == 'line_therapy'] <- 'Treatment.line'
names(dataDF_dammed)[names(dataDF_dammed) == 'bedste_respons'] <- 'Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL'
names(dataDF_dammed)[names(dataDF_dammed) == 'record_id'] <- 'Center.Unique.ID'

#code Treatment line column
dataDF_dammed <- dataDF_dammed %>% dplyr::mutate(
    Treatment.line = case_when(
      Treatment.line == 2  ~ "2",
      Treatment.line >= 3   ~ "3 or higher",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Treatment.line = factor(
      Treatment.line,
      levels = c("2", "3 or higher")
    )
)
# code CNS mets line column
dataDF_dammed <- dataDF_dammed %>% dplyr::mutate(
    CNS.metastases = case_when(
      CNS.metastases == 0  ~ "No",
      CNS.metastases == 1   ~ "Yes",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    CNS.metastases = factor(
      CNS.metastases,
      levels = c("No", "Yes")
    )
)

#keep only relevant columns
common_cols <- intersect(colnames(dataDF_dammed), colnames(dataDF))

dataDF_dammed <- dataDF_dammed[, ..common_cols]

## Find non-Numeric columns
num_cols <- unlist(lapply(dataDF_dammed, is.numeric))         # Identify numeric columns

### NOW MAKE SURE THAT THE COLUMNS ARE IN THE CORRECT FORMAT NEEDED FOR ANALYSIS.
## Numeric columns
dataDF_dammed <- dataDF_dammed %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(numeric_feats),
                ~ as.numeric(as.character(.))))

## Categorical
dataDF_dammed <- dataDF_dammed %>% mutate(across(all_of(categ_feats), as.character))

#remove NAs
dataDF_dammed <- dataDF_dammed %>%
  # 1) if you really want to strip the literal text "NA" out of character columns:
  mutate(across(
    where(is.character),
    ~ str_replace_all(., "\\bNA\\b", "")  # removes the letters NA, but leaves true NA untouched
  )) %>%
  # 2) now drop _entire rows_ that still have any real NA
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.)))

dim(dataDF_dammed)
```

#Cohort joining in one
```{r Cohort joining}
dataDF$Cohort <- "TIL"
dataDF_dammed$Cohort <- "No TIL"

dataDF_merge <- dataDF %>%
  bind_rows(
    dataDF_dammed)
dataDF_merge$Cohort <- as.factor(dataDF_merge$Cohort)
dataDF_merge <- dataDF_merge %>%
  # 1) if you really want to strip the literal text "NA" out of character columns:
  mutate(across(
    where(is.character),
    ~ str_replace_all(., "\\bNA\\b", "")  # removes the letters NA, but leaves true NA untouched
  )) %>%
  # 2) now drop _entire rows_ that still have any real NA
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.)))

## Numeric columns
dataDF_merge <- dataDF_merge %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(numeric_feats),
                ~ as.numeric(as.character(.))))

dataDF_merge <- dataDF_merge %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.character),
      ~ gsub(" ", "_", .)
    )
  )
dataDF_merge <- dataDF_merge %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ gsub(" ", "_", .)))

## FIRST MAKE SURE THERE ARE NO BLANKS ANYWHERE IN THE DATA
## Find non-Numeric columns
num_cols <- unlist(lapply(dataDF_merge, is.numeric))         # Identify numeric columns

### NOW MAKE SURE THAT THE COLUMNS ARE IN THE CORRECT FORMAT NEEDED FOR ANALYSIS.
## Numeric columns
dataDF_merge <- dataDF_merge %>% mutate(across(all_of(numeric_feats), as.numeric))

## Categorical
categ_feats <- c(categ_feats, "Cohort")
dataDF_merge <- dataDF_merge %>% mutate(across(all_of(categ_feats), as.character))

# We need to transform character columns to categorical, to have the different levels
dataDF_merge <- dataDF_merge %>% mutate(across(all_of(categ_feats), as.factor))
dataDF <- dataDF_merge %>% select(all_of(c(colnames(dataDF_merge)[1], OS_time,OS_status, PFS_time,PFS_status, features))) %>% distinct()

```


# Survival analysis using unmatched patient data
## Overall survival
```{r OS unmatched, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=16, fig.height=8, eval=TRUE}
# Survival object
surv_obj <- Surv(dataDF_merge$OS.months, dataDF_merge$OS.event)

# Combine all variables into a data frame
data <- cbind(dataDF_merge, surv_obj)

# Compute the Kaplan-Meier model
fit_overall = survfit(Surv(dataDF_merge$OS.months, dataDF_merge$OS.event) ~ Cohort, data=dataDF_merge)
print(fit_overall)

# Modify the names of the strata to remove "regime_correct="
names(fit_overall$strata) <- sub("Cohort =", " ", names(fit_overall$strata))

OVS_all <- ggsurvfit(fit_overall, size = 1.5)               # Adjust the thickness of the lines here
# add_confidence_interval()

OVS_all +  
  add_censor_mark() +
  add_risktable(size = 5,
                theme = theme_risktable_default(axis.text.y.size = 15,
                                                plot.title.size = 15),
    risktable_stats = "{n.risk} ({cum.event})") + 
  labs( x = "Months", y = "Survival Probability",
        title = "Overall Survival Responders (All responders)"
  ) +
  xlim(0, 120) +                       # Set the limit of the x-axis
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 120, by = 12)) +  # Break the x-axis in multiples of 12 months
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.0),  # Set y-axis breaks
    limits = c(0, 1)                     # Ensure y-axis limits include all breaks
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + 
  theme_classic() +  # Apply the classic theme
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 18),  # Adjust title size
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20),  # Adjust X label size
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20),  # Adjust Y label size
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 15),  # Adjust X-axis tick label size
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15),   # Adjust Y-axis tick label size
    legend.position   = "bottom",
    legend.direction  = "horizontal",
    legend.text       = element_text(size = 18),
    legend.key.size   = unit(10, "bigpts"),
    legend.title      = element_blank(),
  )

# Save the plot to the result folder
# Save the OVS plot to the result folder
# file_name_ovs <- file.path(path.expand(result), "Overall_Survival_plot_all.png")  # Define the file path
#ggsave(file_name_ovs, plot = OVS_all, width = 16, height = 12, units = "in", dpi = 300)  # Save the plot as a PNG file

```

# Propensity Score Matching for Treatment Groups Based on Clinical Features
## Matching with standardized caliper
```{r,warning=F, message=F, fig.width=16, fig.height=8,eval=TRUE}
matching_features <- paste0("`", setdiff(features, c("Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL")), "`", collapse = " + ")
matching_formula <- as.formula(paste0("Cohort ~", matching_features))

comparisons <- list(c("No_TIL", "TIL"))

names(dataDF_merge)[names(dataDF_merge) == 'OS.months'] <- 'OS_months'
names(dataDF_merge)[names(dataDF_merge) == 'OS.event'] <- 'Dead'
names(dataDF_merge)[names(dataDF_merge) == 'PFS.months'] <- 'PFS_months'
names(dataDF_merge)[names(dataDF_merge) == 'PFS.event'] <- 'Progressed'

OS_psm_all <- run_psm_and_survival(dataDF = dataDF_merge, comparisons = comparisons,covariate_to_split = "Cohort", endpoint = "OS", truncate_month = 60)
PFS_psm_all <- run_psm_and_survival(dataDF = dataDF_merge, comparisons = comparisons,covariate_to_split = "Cohort", endpoint = "PFS", truncate_month = 60)

OS_psm_all$surv_plots
PFS_psm_all$surv_plots
```


# Clinical characterization of the propensity-matched cohorts
## Median OS and PFS tables
```{r,warning=F, message=F, fig.width=16, fig.height=8,eval=TRUE}
matched_ids <- OS_psm_all$matched_dfs[[1]]$Center.Unique.ID
df_matched <- subset(dataDF_merge,Center.Unique.ID %in% matched_ids )

df_matched <- df_matched %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(c("OS_months", "Dead", "PFS_months", "Progressed")),
      as.numeric
    )
  )

fit_OS_matched <- survfit(
  Surv(df_matched$OS_months, df_matched$Dead) ~ 1,
  data=df_matched
)

fit_OS_matched_treatment <- survfit(
  Surv(df_matched$OS_months, df_matched$Dead) ~ Cohort,
  data=df_matched
)

fit_PFS_matched <- survfit(
  Surv(PFS_months, Progressed) ~ 1,
  data = df_matched
)

fit_PFS_matched_treatment <- survfit(
  Surv(PFS_months, Progressed) ~ Cohort,
  data = df_matched
)

# Helper function
extract_median_survival <- function(fit, endpoint, stratified = FALSE) {
  
  x <- summary(fit)$table
  
  if (!stratified) {
    data.frame(
      Endpoint = endpoint,
      Group = "Overall matched cohort",
      Median = x["median"],
      `95% CI` = sprintf("%.1f–%.1f", x["0.95LCL"], x["0.95UCL"]),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  } else {
    data.frame(
      Endpoint = endpoint,
      Group = sub(".*=", "", rownames(x)),
      Median = x[, "median"],
      `95% CI` = sprintf("%.1f–%.1f", x[, "0.95LCL"], x[, "0.95UCL"]),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }
}

# Combine results
survival_summary <- bind_rows(
  extract_median_survival(fit_OS_matched, "Overall survival (OS)"),
  extract_median_survival(fit_OS_matched_treatment, "Overall survival (OS)", TRUE),
  extract_median_survival(fit_PFS_matched, "Progression-free survival (PFS)"),
  extract_median_survival(fit_PFS_matched_treatment, "Progression-free survival (PFS)", TRUE)
)

# Pretty Markdown table
kable(
  survival_summary,
  row.names = F,
  digits = 1,
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Median survival in the propensity score–matched cohort"
)
```

##BOR distribution
```{r,fig.width=16, fig.height=8,eval=TRUE}
## OR distribution
table(df_matched$Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL)
table(df_matched$Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL, df_matched$Cohort)

#presented as piechart
pie_overall <- df_matched %>%
  filter(!is.na(Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL)) %>%
  count(Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL) %>%
  mutate(
    pct = n / sum(n) * 100,
    label = paste0(Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL, "\n", n, " (", round(pct, 1), "%)")
  )

ggplot(pie_overall, aes(x = "", y = n, fill = Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, color = "white") +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "Best overall response to BRAF/MEKi",
    fill = "Response"
  ) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 4)+
   theme(strip.text = element_text(size=20),
        title = element_text(size = 20))

### BOR by cohort
pie_by_cohort <- df_matched %>%
  filter(!is.na(Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL), !is.na(Cohort)) %>%
  count(Cohort, Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL) %>%
  group_by(Cohort) %>%
  mutate(
    pct = n / sum(n) * 100,
    label = paste0(Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL, "\n", n, " (", round(pct, 1), "%)")
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(pie_by_cohort, aes(x = "", y = n, fill = Best.response.to.BRAFi.post.TIL)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, color = "white") +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  facet_wrap(~ Cohort) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "Best overall response to BRAF/MEKi, stratified by response",
    fill = "Response"
  ) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3.5)+
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size=20),
        title = element_text(size = 20))
```
